newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sweden criticises EU use of anti-dumping weapon.
newsitem.headline: Sweden criticises EU use of anti-dumping weapon.

text.p: Free-trade enthusiast Sweden criticised the European Union's anti-dumping policies on Monday, saying the 15-nation bloc slapped import duties on cheaper foreign products too often.
Trade Minister Leig Pagrotsky raised the issue in talks with EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan.
"This is the last remaining major protectionist instrument (the EU) has," Pagrotsky told journalists. "We want it to be used much less frequently."
"We in Sweden are very sceptical about it," he added.
When Sweden entered the EU in 1995, it had no anti-dumping duties in force. But following membership, there were now about 70, Pagrotsky said.
He told Brittan anti-dumping duties were contrary to the EU's interest, saying that they are "tantamount to a tax on our consumers".
He specifically raised the case of import duties on handbags from China, an industrial sector which he said was undergoing important structural changes.
Production of simple types of handbags was being located to low-cost countries while activities such as product development, design, marketing and administration were retained in the EU.
"This development in my view represents a sound and rational adaptation and I think it is a mistake to try to prevent it through anti-dumping measures," Pagrotsky said in a statement.
Last month, the EU executive introduced anti-dumping duties of nearly 40 percent on imports of handbags from China.
Following a complaint in March last year by the European Committee for Leather Goods Industries, the Commission said it had evidence Chinese manufacturers were dumping handbags in Europe.
But Pagrotsky said the case was badly founded.
He said there had been some positive changes in the anti-dumping policies of the European Commission, among other things referring to the treatement of non-market economies.
"We appreciate your efforts highly and we fully understand that it is not easy to initiate these changes, given the sharply contrasting views among member states," he said in the statement.
